paper_diagnosis: Acute hepatitis E in a young male

demographics.location_context: nearby village area near Multan, Pakistan

presentation_summary: 30-year-old man presented with sudden progressive yellow discoloration of the eyes for three days and dark-colored urine for the past few days.

He also had dull mild abdominal pain, loss of appetite, nausea, and one non-bloody vomiting episode; he denied pruritus, clay-colored stool, diarrhea, abdominal distension, decreased urine output, bleeding, joint pain, alcohol, drugs, surgery, transfusion, dental extraction, IV drug use, and illicit sexual behavior.
He drank unfiltered water and reported poor sanitary conditions at home.
Exam showed yellow sclera, mild epigastric and right hypochondrial tenderness, no flapping tremor, no visceromegaly, no shifting dullness, and otherwise normal examination.

Labs showed hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, WBC 10.3 x10^9/L, platelets 185 x10^9/L, total bilirubin 10.6 mg/dL, conjugated bilirubin 6.4 mg/dL, unconjugated bilirubin 4.1 mg/dL, ALT 1783 U/L, AST 1591 U/L, ALP 183 U/L, gamma GT 86 U/L, albumin 3.5 g/dL, PT 16 seconds, INR 1.5, creatinine 0.7 mg/dL, BUN 10 mg/dL, sodium 137 mmol/L, potassium 3.8 mmol/L, bicarbonate 22 mmol/L, amylase 55 U/L, and lipase 14 U/L.
Viral serology showed reactive anti-HEV IgM; anti-HAV IgM, HBsAg, and anti-HCV were nonreactive.
Abdominal ultrasound showed gallbladder wall thickening with normal liver and spleen.

He was hospitalized briefly for poor oral intake and received IV dextrose-containing fluids, IV proton pump inhibitor, IV antiemetics, and lactulose syrup; nausea improved, oral intake returned, enzymes began to normalize, and follow-up at two weeks and one month showed complete symptom and liver-enzyme normalization.
